output:
Dear all,

Just coming up for air after nights, and I’ve been looking forward to replying. Amma and Appa, I’m genuinely thrilled you’re coming. Having you here for the summer, with ordinary days together rather than trying to fit everything into a short visit, means so much to me. Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable, including “Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays”. No pressure, Amma.

Kiran, you’re right that I should have told you earlier. I started the visa paperwork because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, and I should have looped you in then. I didn’t, and that’s on me. I’m sorry you heard about it only once things were under way.

For a little background, the idea first came up on the phone in August, when Rohan was showing Appa the vegetable patch on video and Appa said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” I was delighted, and we kept talking about it. That doesn’t excuse my not speaking to you.

Your concerns about Appa’s heart are important, and I don’t want my being a doctor to stand in for a proper plan. Dr. Prakash has agreed to review Appa in March before they fly, and to do a video consultation in July. He’s also happy to share his notes with me, with Appa’s agreement, so we can keep his care joined up.

I’ve had a travel insurance quote of about £640 each for the six months, including pre-existing cardiac cover. The agent says Appa’s stent is covered, but I’ll get that confirmed in the policy wording, along with the limits and exclusions, before we buy it. We shouldn’t assume visitor treatment on the NHS would be free. Leicester Royal is fifteen minutes from the house, and I know many of the cardiology team, which is reassuring, but it isn’t a substitute for insurance or Dr. Prakash being happy for Appa to travel.

The annexe at the back is finished: ground floor, no steps, and their own shower with a grab rail. They’ll have their own space rather than having to live around our household timetable.

On the dates, this is the UK long-term visitor visa, with a maximum of six months per visit. The plan is the first week of April to the end of September 2027; we’ll check the exact dates stay within that limit.

And yes, six months is a big change for Amma when six weeks has been her longest stay away since Paati died. Amma, you don’t have to promise now that you’ll enjoy every minute or stay until September. The return ticket will be flexible, and you can go home whenever you want. I want this to be something you enjoy, not something you feel obliged to see through.

Pune and Ganesh Chaturthi needn’t be lost either. One possibility is for Amma and Appa to leave Leicester in September, fly to Pune for the festival and finish the trip there. Or would the Pune lot like to come here in August? I’d be very happy to cover your flights. It wouldn’t be the same as having them in Pune for Ganesh Chaturthi, but it could give us some lovely time together.

Could we all have a video call this Sunday at 4 pm UK / 9.30 pm India? I’d like us to talk this through properly, hear what Amma and Appa want, and make room for everyone’s worries and suggestions.

Love,
Meera
